open-question.question: Does docs/design-claims.md change in this milestone to reflect the new identity (for example its intro, or the standing of claims 1 and 14), or is it left untouched as the unchanged evidence the pitch links to?
open-question.recommendation: The page is the evidence the pitch links to and is worth most unrewritten: its claims, numbers, and anchors stay valid for the README and for every claim reference in milestone history, and the goal does not list it. Pointing out which claims carry the identity is the README's job, not the evidence page's.
open-question.alternative: docs/design-claims.md does not change in this milestone. The intro stays as it is. Claims 1 and 14 keep their wording, their numbers, and their places in the "Decisions" and "Efficiency" groups. All 19 claims and their anchors stay the same. The page remains the unchanged evidence that the pitch surfaces link to. This is a "never in this milestone" choice: a later change is left to whatever milestone next touches the claims, for example one that measures claim 1. It matches the goal's list of surfaces exactly, because that list leaves out docs/design-claims.md. The page's measured, ASD-STE100 claims stay apart from the full-strength pitch, so a reader who follows a link from the pitch finds evidence that the reframe has not rewritten. Every existing anchor stays valid, and so does every "claim N" reference in milestone history. The page about what Cairn claims does not show which of its claims the new identity rests on. Claims 1 and 14 stay among nineteen without emphasis, in two different groups, so the pitch and its evidence page lead with different things. Whether that matters depends on the "Design principles selection" sibling, which decides whether the README links those two claims at all.

The intro paragraph of docs/design-claims.md gains a sentence or two. They name claim 1 ("Cairn finds the open questions before the work starts.") and claim 14 ("Unattended batch runs are possible.") as the two claims Cairn's identity rests on, and link to each. Nothing else on the page changes. The claim headings, their wording, the numbering, the six groups, the Design and Metric lines, and the existing sentence that only claim 11's test runs all stay as they are. The evidence page shows which claims the new identity rests on, at the cost of one intro edit. No numbering, anchor, or claim text changes, so the README's existing #2, #5, and #11 links and every historical "claim N" reference in milestones/ stay correct. It adds a page the goal does not list to the milestone's scope. It points at the identity without saying anything about its strength: the pitch says "all the important questions", and claim 1's metric counts planted gaps that nothing measures yet. Readers have to infer that gap from the existing claim-11-only sentence. Whether the page should bridge that gap depends on the "Claim strength disclosure" sibling.

The intro gains the same sentences that name claims 1 and 14 as the base of the identity. The heading and Design text of those two claims are also reworded in place, in the page's ASD-STE100 register, to use the pitch's terms. Claim 1 speaks of bringing the important questions up to be decided before the work starts. Claim 14 speaks of handing long-running execution to agents with no user turns. The two claims keep their numbers and their groups, and no other claim changes. Their heading anchors change with the new wording, and any inbound link to them is updated. The pitch and its evidence page describe the identity in the same words, so a reader who follows a link from the one-liner lands on a claim that states the same promise. The page then reads as the backing for the new identity, not only for the old milestone-driven framing. It rewrites two measured claims toward pitch wording, so they are no longer the unchanged evidence. It risks making claim 1 match "all the important questions" while its metric and the claim-11-only test coverage stay the same, which widens the gap the page records. It also changes the claims' heading anchors, which the "Design principles selection" sibling may be about to link from the README, and it ties the claims' wording to the "Identity one-liner wording" sibling's outcome.

The page is restructured to lead with the identity. Claims 1 and 14 move into a new first group that the identity heads, and the claims are renumbered to follow the new order. The intro's group count and description are updated to match, and anchored inbound links (the README's design-principles links) are rewritten to the new anchors. The wording of the claims and their Design and Metric lines stays the same. The page's own structure carries the identity: the first claims a reader sees are the two the pitch rests on, side by side. The pitch and its evidence page then have the same shape without any change to what a claim says. Renumbering breaks the "claim N" references that the history in milestones/README.md and earlier milestone records use (claims 2, 5, 11, and 12 among them), and those records are never rewritten. It also changes every heading anchor that follows from a number, which forces README link edits. It is the largest change, to a page the goal does not list, and its value depends on whether the "Design principles selection" sibling brings claims 1 and 14 forward on the README.
